description: This case study is an open access paper in Oxford Open Energy, published on 21 November 2024, that develops a transition pathway for the low-emission district heating system of Helsinki, Finland. It proposes a transition management model in which the city decentralises heat supply through heat auctions that give third parties access to the network, open energy mapping and faster permitting, supported by heat pumps, demand response, energy storage and grid strengthening. The work combines energy system modelling, environmental and economic assessment with the ENVIMAT input-output model, and a co-creation process of fifteen expert workshops held between August 2020 and January 2021. Access: free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; Helsinki energy system data are public on the city's energy challenge site and further modelling data are available from the corresponding author on request. Coverage is the city of Helsinki. Caveats: only the abstract and data statement were read, so quantitative results are not summarised. It suits adaptation planning and capacity planning studies of urban district heating, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
